step1_analysis.description: A passive LC network forming a bandpass filter. In the original paper, this passive structure is combined with an active Q-enhancement negative resistance circuit (cross-coupled pair) to compensate for inductor losses and achieve 0-dB insertion loss.

paper_reference.title: A 0-dB IL 2140 30 MHz Bandpass Filter Utilizing Q-Enhanced Spiral Inductors in Standard CMOS

center_frequency.description: The frequency at which the filter has minimum insertion loss (peak gain).

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the LC tank resonance f = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L * C)). Assuming L~2nH and C~2.7pF for the tank.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The center frequency is primarily determined by passive component values, which can be scaled to match the 2.14 GHz target regardless of the technology node.

insertion_loss.description: The loss of signal power resulting from the insertion of the filter, measured at the center frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: Without the active Q-enhancement circuit (which is missing from this passive netlist), the insertion loss will be strictly negative due to finite Q of the passives.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper achieves 0 dB by using a negative resistance generator. Since this netlist only contains the passive elements, standard on-chip inductor Q-factors (typically 5-10) will result in significant insertion loss.

bandwidth.description: The 3-dB passband width of the filter.

sky130_expected.reasoning: The bandwidth depends on the filter order and loaded Q. Without Q-enhancement, the bandwidth might be wider than the reported 60 MHz due to lower effective Q.

step3_testbench.description: AC analysis to measure the frequency response, center frequency, and insertion loss of the passive bandpass filter.
